claims.statement: The Agent Server image is built from the uv workspace and lockfile: langgraph.json sets source.kind to uv with root '.' and package langchain-chess-server, Python 3.13 on the wolfi distro, graph chess from apps/server graph.py:make_graph and http.app from apps/server app.py:app.

Because langgraph-cli copies only the root pyproject.toml before uv export (the server README cites 0.4.31; the root dev group pins 0.4.40), langgraph.json dockerfile_lines ADDs member pyproject.toml files into /tmp/uv_export/project; it lists libs/chess, libs/systemone, libs/cli and apps/server but not evals, even though evals is a root workspace member and the README says the list must stay in step with the workspace members.

The root pyproject.toml is a virtual workspace whose [tool.uv.sources] marks all five distributions (including langchain-chess-evals) as workspace = true; member manifests carry no workspace sources because each member is installed on its own in the image and a member-level workspace source fails there.

mise run build runs `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vp build`, whose Vite config takes base from BASE_PATH (default /ui/) and outDir from OUT_DIR (default apps/server/langchain_chess_server/static); mise run deploy no longer builds the UI and only runs `langgraph deploy --no-remote --agent-id langchain-chess --agent-environment production --deployment-type dev`, with a comment that deploys should come from CI because langgraph deploy sends .env as the deployment's secrets.

The server mounts the static UI at /ui only when the static directory exists; otherwise /ui/ returns a 404 JSON telling the user to run mise run build, and in the deployed image the directory is absent because GitHub Pages hosts the UI, while the /ui JSON routes still answer.

.dockerignore limits the build context to the uv workspace and excludes tests, apps/web, apps/review, packages, .github and secret files such as .env; a gitignored static directory present in the build directory would still enter the image (Docker semantics only), but the CI agent job installs no web dependencies and no longer builds the UI, so its header comment claiming CI relies on the static build is out of date.

deploy.yml (agent), pages.yml (web UI) and deploy-review.yml (review) each run on push to main filtered by on.push.paths and on workflow_dispatch without inputs, which ignores the path filters; the jobs run only on refs/heads/main, so a dispatch from another branch skips.

The agent workflow's path filter covers libs/chess, libs/systemone, libs/cli/pyproject.toml, apps/server, uv.lock, pyproject.toml, .python-version, langgraph.json, .dockerignore and scripts/agent-tags.sh but no longer apps/web, packages/chess-ui or JS files; the pages workflow covers apps/web, packages/chess-ui and the shared JS files; the review workflow covers apps/review, packages/chess-ui and the shared JS files; all include mise.toml, mise.lock, the setup action, ci.yml, their own workflow file and scripts/superseded.sh.

Each deploy workflow (agent, review, grader) calls ci.yml as a reusable workflow with ref set to the tip SHA, and the deploy job needs both tip and ci, so merges deploy only behind the same checks pull requests run, on the exact commit that is deployed.

The agent deploy job sets up without web dependencies, writes a .env with LANGSMITH_GATEWAY, LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_API_KEY, TYPESAFE_BASE_URL and TYPESAFE_API_KEY (keys from the LC_GATEWAY_KEY secret) because langgraph deploy re-sends the env file as the revision's secrets on every deploy, then, unless superseded, runs mise run deploy -- --no-input (image only) and mise run agent:tag, both with the LANGSMITH_API_KEY secret.

The review app is published by a separate deploy-review.yml whose tip job requires main and a non-empty CUSTOM_APP_ID repository variable; unless superseded, the review job writes apps/review/.langsmith/app.json from that variable (name langchain-chess-review) and runs langsmith apps push with LANGSMITH_API_KEY.

Each deploy workflow holds a workflow-level concurrency group per ref (deploy-agent-<ref>, deploy-review-<ref>) with queue: max, so the whole run including CI is serialized in push order and a newer run never cancels a pending deploy; ci.yml instead uses a group keyed on PR number or run id with cancel-in-progress true, so a new merge never cancels a deploy's checks.

ci.yml runs on pull requests (ignoring markdown, plans and openwiki changes) and on workflow_call with an optional ref input; a python job runs mise run check:python and test:python, a web job runs check:web, test:web and review:size (the review app upload budget check), and an e2e job installs Chromium and runs mise run test:e2e.

The shared setup action installs mise tools behind Socket Firewall, runs uv sync --all-packages --all-groups --locked (failing on a stale uv.lock) and pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, and saves package caches only on main while other refs only restore.
A local image smoke build is run with `uv run --all-packages langgraph build -t langchain-chess:smoke`, and deploying needs Docker with buildx because the image is built locally.

The server's custom app registers /ui/config (graph id, ChessContext JSON schema and defaults) and /ui/model (max_input_tokens and takes_effort for a required model query parameter) regardless of whether the static build exists, and redirects a bare /ui to /ui/.
The UI is mounted with app.mount rather than app.frontend() because frontend routes are low priority and the Agent Server's own /ui mount would otherwise answer first.

ServerSettings reads the shell then .env and rejects LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_API_KEY, TYPESAFE_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_BASE_URL when set but blank; make_graph constructs ServerSettings for each run (calls without an execution runtime get a credential-free shape graph), so an empty value written into the deployment .env fails runs rather than falling back silently.

The first job of each deploy workflow (agent, review, grader), tip, runs inside the workflow's queued concurrency lock and resolves the current main commit via the GitHub API rather than using the pushed SHA, so a retried or long-queued older run ships main as it is now, and CI and the deploy checkout both use that SHA.

Before deploying, each deploy job (agent, pages, review, grader) fetches current main and runs scripts/superseded.sh, which reads the workflow's on.push.paths from main's copy, converts them to :(glob) pathspecs and diffs the tested SHA against main; on a matching change the job skips the deploy step with a notice if a newer non-cancelled run of the same workflow exists on main, and otherwise fails asking to re-run all jobs, so a deploy-only re-run cannot ship a stale commit.

Replacing a pending older run in a deploy concurrency group is safe only because every run of that workflow deploys the same target, which is why the review app lives in its own workflow and group instead of sharing the agent's.

No deploy workflow's on.push.paths (agent, pages, review, grader) includes evals/**, so changes confined to the evals workspace member never redeploy anything; only shared root files such as pyproject.toml and uv.lock trigger the agent and grader workflows, while CI still checks and tests evals.

deploy-grader.yml rebuilds the langchain-chess-grader sandbox snapshot on main pushes touching libs/chess, libs/systemone, libs/cli, uv.lock, pyproject.toml, .python-version, docker/grader.Dockerfile or scripts/grader-snapshot.py, running scripts/grader-snapshot.py with LANGSMITH_API_KEY and the optional LANGSMITH_WORKSPACE_ID variable; the build runs in a LangSmith sandbox so the runner needs no Docker.

grader-snapshot.py stages grader.Dockerfile, wheels of langchain-chess, langchain-chess-systemone and langchain-chess-cli, and a requirements.txt from uv export --package langchain-chess-cli --frozen --no-dev --no-emit-workspace, then builds the snapshot via SandboxClient tagged latest; the Dockerfile installs a SHA-256-verified Stockfish 19 and the requirements plus wheels into /opt/lcchess with STOCKFISH_PATH set.

pages.yml publishes the web UI to GitHub Pages: its tip job requires main and a non-empty VITE_API_URL repository variable; the build job runs vp build in apps/web with BASE_PATH=/<repo>/, OUT_DIR=dist and VITE_API_URL, uploads apps/web/dist as a Pages artifact, and a deploy job (skipped when superseded) runs configure-pages and deploy-pages in the github-pages environment; its concurrency group is pages-<ref> with queue: max.

Changing VITE_API_URL touches no watched path, so the Pages site must be republished by dispatching pages.yml manually; the built UI uses VITE_API_URL as its API base so it talks to the deployed agent.

mise run agent:tag (scripts/agent-tags.sh) looks up the langchain-chess agent via the langsmith CLI and tags the langchain-chess-positions dataset (when it exists) and each environment's tracing project with the agent's tag value; tagging upserts, so CI re-tags after every agent deploy.
